message.content: {"caption":"Annotated shopping-results screenshot showing an overly broad Sony headphone search and suggested ways to narrow it.","description":"A composite explanatory diagram has an e-commerce search-results screenshot on the left and a text panel on the right. In the screenshot, the search field contains “Bluetooth headphones Sony,” outlined in red. A red box also highlights the result count, which reads “Items 1–12 of 5758,” and the red annotation “Too many items to browse” points out the large result set. The page includes a “Shop By” sidebar with shopping options and category filters, related search terms, a “Sort by” control set to “Relevance,” and product listings. Four prominent listings show over-ear headphones (the fourth listing also displays accessories); product titles, ratings, review counts, and prices appear beneath them, but most of that small text is not readable. Add-to-cart buttons are visible. Near the bottom, two black rectangular product images are boxed in red and identified by the red label “Irrelevant objects.” No arrows or other directional connections are shown. The right panel is headed “Diagnose the trajectory:” and says, “The agent spent endless steps on ‘page next’, which exhausts the interaction limits without providing the requested information from user. …” A horizontal divider separates this from “Distilled strategies to ReasoningBank:” followed by three recommendations: “Search query optimization” to avoid irrelevance and ensure preciseness; “Adjust number of items displayed per page” to accelerate; and “Use filters available.”","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
